$comment: Design v3.1 §1 — the registry of every TOP-LEVEL entry that appears under the daemon state home (crewStateHome(): the --db parent, ~/.wicked-crew by default). wicked-core embeds this file (src/state_home.rs, include_str!) to build the worker Read fence: one deny rule per entry, with the resolved skills/snapshots/<gen>/ the ONLY non-denied path. At every launch that opens the fence, core LISTS the state home's top-level entries (and skills/'s) and REFUSES the launch, naming the entry, if one is not classified here — fail closed, never widen. No runtime enumeration ever BUILDS a rule; this list is static. crew mirrors this file at packages/crew/tests/fixtures/state-home-subtrees.json, and its tests/state-home-subtrees.test.ts asserts (a) every join(<state home>, …) in crew's src/ names an entry here and (b) a booted daemon creates nothing outside it. `name` is an exact top-level name; `prefix` covers a file and its sidecars (core.db, core.db-wal, core.db.events, …). `worker_read` is prose for the reader; the skills entry's `read_slot` and `denied_children` are the machine-readable half core enforces. Design v3.3 §1: skills/snapshots/ is the ONE directory core lists at launch to BUILD rules — one deny per sibling entry (every generation but the handed one; every .staging-*/.tmp-current-* entry), failing closed on an unlistable slot or an entry that is neither a generation directory (decimal digits, as crew publishes them) nor a recognised staging name. Design v3.5 §2: the skills entry lists EVERY name the store can ever create under skills/ — settled AND transient (.staging-* park-and-place directories, manifest.json.tmp-* commit files, snapshots/.staging-* generations being written, snapshots/.tmp-current-* links before their rename, the refused/ sentinel that is named but never created) — because a launch admitted while a mutation is parked must classify every child it sees; `denied_children_kinds` records each pattern's kind and whether it is transient (src/skills/root-names.ts is crew's source of truth; tests/skills-fence-names.test.ts asserts equality and observes the transient names mid-mutation). Residuals (documented): a top-level entry created under the state home WHILE a session is running is fenced at the next launch, not mid-session — crew is the only writer of that directory; a generation published while a session runs is readable by that session until its next launch (generations are immutable and hold only the enabled skills of a newer publish). core#411 / crew#497 (F-RC1-011, F-RC2-020): an entry this registry does not classify is a CONFIGURATION error, not a worker failure — core surveys the state home at INTAKE (`Core::launch_run` refuses synchronously with a typed `StateHomeConfigError` naming every unregistered entry and the remedy; no session is persisted, nothing plans, no triage judge) and exposes the same survey as `preflight_state_home` / core-ts `Core.preflightStateHome` for crew's boot; crew runs it at `serve`, reports `GET /diagnostics.stateHome`, warns on `GET /health`, and answers `POST /runs` 409 until the entry is gone. Entries carrying an `env` field are placed by an OPERATOR variable, not by a `join(<state home>, …)` in crew's src/ (`workflows`, `steering-inbox`): registered so a pre-existing placement is fenced rather than refusing every launch, while crew refuses to boot with that variable pointed inside the state home. There is deliberately NO pattern entry for debris (`skills.fixture-debris-*` and the like): a quarantine-by-rename INSIDE the state home is exactly what the fence must refuse — move it out.
